alternate_names: Gaya of the South (epithet of Avani itself)
deities: Ramalingeshwara (Shiva; linga consecrated by Lord Rama - presiding)
Sita Devi (hilltop shrine - one of the very few Sita temples in India)
festivals: Annual Ramalingeshwara festival with Agra Archana to 'Hari Shresta Adi Jambava' (per a local account - verify)

history.dynasty: Nolamba dynasty (10th century); earliest Shatrughneshvara shrine attributed to the Western Gangas of Talakad (per art historian James Harle, based on a Ganga inscription); partial Chola renovation; main mandapam and rajagopuram built by the Vijayanagara kings
history.period: Early 10th century (per art historian Madhusudan Dhaky); an ASI-noted inscription at Avani is dated 399 AD; later inscriptions call Avani the 'Gaya of the South'
history.summary: The Ramalingeshwara group of temples at Avani village (Mulbagal taluk) is an ASI-protected monument of national importance and a fine example of Nolamba Dravida architecture. Legend holds Avani (from 'earth'; Sita is Avanisuta, 'daughter of earth') as the site of Valmiki's ashram where Sita lived in exile and gave birth to Lava and Kusha - the adjacent hill is still called Lava-Kusha Betta, and a rare hilltop Sita Devi shrine marks where tradition says Sita entered the earth. After Rama's Ashwamedha horse was stopped by Lava and Kusha and Rama ended up fighting his own sons, Valmiki advised expiation (papa parihara): Rama, Lakshmana, Bharata and Shatrughna each installed a linga here - the four shrines of the complex. Art-historically, the walled enclosure (prakara) with the Shatrughneshvara and Lakshmanalingeshwara shrines is among the earliest such grouped-shrine complexes in Karnataka. A later tradition records that Sri Narasimha Bharati IV of the Sringeri Sharada Peetham, camping at Avani, found a standing Sharada idol and established the Avani Sringeri Jagadguru Shankaracharya Sharada Peetham matha here (per a local account - verify). CSV town/state (Kolar, Karnataka) are correct, with Avani village near Mulbagal as the precise location.

name: Avani (Ramalingeshwara Group of Temples)
town_description: Avani is a small heritage village in Mulbagal taluk, Kolar district - about 30 km from Kolar and 95 km from Bengaluru - set at the foot of Avani Betta (also called Lava-Kusha Betta), a popular rock-climbing and trekking spot. The 10th-century Ramalingeshwara temple complex stands at the foothill with the hilltop Sita temple above; the plateau beside the temples is traditionally identified as Valmiki's abode.

travel.airport: Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru - about 95-100 km.
travel.railway: Nearest stations at Mulbagal/Kolar (verify); Bengaluru City Junction is the major railhead (~95 km).
travel.road: About 30 km from Kolar and 95 km from Bengaluru; the temple complex is at the foot of Avani Betta, reachable by road with local taxis from Mulbagal/Kolar.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; combine with the Avani Betta trek in the cooler months.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open daily as an ASI-protected monument (typical hours 6:00 AM - 6:00 PM - verify). Videography is not allowed inside the shrines per visitor accounts; the complex is well maintained by the Archaeological Department.
